parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A beam PQ is clamped so that the beam is horizontal. A mass $M$ of 500 g is hung from end Q and the beam bends slightly, as illustrated in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1.png}}

The length $l$ of the beam from the edge of the clamp R to end Q is 60.0 cm. The width $b$ of the beam is 30.0 mm and the thickness $d$ of the beam is 5.00 mm. The material of the beam has Young modulus $E$.

The mass $M$ is made to oscillate vertically. The time period $T$ of the oscillations is 0.58 s.

The period $T$ is given by the expression

$$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{4Ml^3}{Ebd^3}}.$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)1
parts.stem: The quantities used to determine $E$ should be measured with accuracy and with precision.
parts.text: Explain the difference between accuracy and precision.

parts.label: (b)(ii)2
parts.text: In a particular experiment, the quantities l and T are measured with the same percentage uncertainty. State and explain which of these two quantities contributes more to the uncertainty in the value of E.
